executive_summary: This portfolio of 11 legacy services is in a Critical modernization state. 10 of 11 services are classified as Not Ready across the majority of modernization pathways, with only the monolith e-commerce application showing partial readiness in containers and managed databases. The portfolio spans 9 distinct technology stacks including mainframe COBOL, Visual Basic 6.0, ColdFusion 8, Java 5/6 on Solaris, Python 2.7, Ruby 1.8, C++ CGI, Node.js 0.10, and ASP.NET WebForms 2.0. Every service except the PHP 8.2 monolith runs on end-of-life runtimes with no security patch availability. No service has a CI/CD pipeline, automated testing, or observability. Portfolio-scale modernization is required across all seven pathways with priority on security remediation, EOL runtime upgrades, and establishing modern DevOps foundations.

Hardcoded configuration and credentials in all 11 services
No health check or readiness endpoints in any service
No API layer or service decomposition in 8 of 11 services
Tight coupling to proprietary or legacy infrastructure

3 services (pricing-cgi, shipping-api, monolith) have basic containerization artifacts
Legacy runtimes (VB6, COBOL, Java 5/6, .NET 2.0) cannot run in standard containers
No container orchestration in most services
Platform dependencies (Windows, Solaris, z/OS) prevent Linux containerization
Heavy proprietary vendor lock-in: Oracle DB (2 services), IBM DB2/z/OS (1), Microsoft SQL Server (3), Microsoft Access (1)
Proprietary runtimes: VB6, ColdFusion, WebLogic, JBoss AS, .NET Framework 2.0, IBM COBOL
Only the monolith (PHP 8.2/MySQL) uses a fully open-source stack
EOL proprietary software with no migration path in place across 10 services
6 distinct database engines requiring migration: Oracle 11g (2), SQL Server 2005/2012 (4), Microsoft Access (1), IBM DB2 (1), MongoDB 2.4 (1), flat files (1)
Hardcoded database credentials in all 11 services
No connection pooling in 8 services
SQL injection vulnerabilities in 6 services
Only monolith uses a managed database (RDS MySQL)

No analytics or reporting infrastructure in 10 of 11 services

No event streaming or change data capture

No infrastructure as code in 10 services (monolith has CloudFormation but no pipeline)
No observability stack (logging, metrics, tracing) in any service
Manual deployment processes across all services

critical_security_findings: SQL injection vulnerabilities in 6 services (crm-desktop, document-portal, helpdesk-tickets, loan-calculator, timesheet-webforms, monolith)
Hardcoded credentials in source control in all 11 services
End-of-life runtimes with known unpatched CVEs in 10 services
No encryption at rest for PII data (payroll-system)

technology_stack_inventory.eol_status: All components EOL or nearing EOL
No framework EOL but architecture is legacy

phase_1.name: Security Remediation and Critical Risk Reduction
actions: Remove all hardcoded credentials from source control and implement AWS Secrets Manager
Fix SQL injection vulnerabilities in 6 affected services
Address XSS and buffer overflow vulnerabilities
Encrypt PII data at rest (payroll system)
Enforce transport security (HTTPS) across all services

phase_2.name: End-of-Life Runtime Migration
actions: Migrate Python 2.7 to Python 3.11+ (helpdesk-tickets)
Migrate Node.js 0.10 to Node.js 20+ LTS (shipping-api)
Migrate Java 5/6 to Java 17+ LTS (loan-calculator, partner-soap)
Migrate Ruby 1.8.7 to Ruby 3.2+ (storefront-rails)
Plan rewrites for VB6 (crm-desktop), ColdFusion 8 (document-portal), .NET 2.0 (timesheet-webforms)
Initiate mainframe modernization assessment for COBOL payroll system
Rewrite C++ CGI as modern microservice (pricing-cgi)

phase_3.name: Database Modernization
actions: Migrate Oracle 11g to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (loan-calculator, partner-soap)
Migrate SQL Server 2005/2012 to Amazon RDS (document-portal, timesheet-webforms, crm-desktop)
Migrate IBM DB2 z/OS to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (payroll-system)
Migrate MongoDB 2.4 to Amazon DocumentDB (shipping-api)
Migrate PostgreSQL 9.1 to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL 15+ (helpdesk-tickets)
Migrate MySQL 5.1 to Amazon Aurora MySQL (storefront-rails)
Migrate flat file to Amazon DynamoDB (pricing-cgi)
Replace Microsoft Access with Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (crm-desktop)

phase_4.name: Containerization and Cloud-Native Architecture
actions: Containerize all modernized services with Docker
Deploy to Amazon ECS or Amazon EKS
Implement service decomposition for the monolith
Establish API gateway patterns for inter-service communication
Implement event-driven architecture with Amazon EventBridge

phase_5.name: Modern DevOps Foundation
actions: Implement CI/CD pipelines with AWS CodePipeline and CodeBuild
Establish automated testing (unit, integration, end-to-end)
Adopt infrastructure as code with AWS CDK or CloudFormation
Implement observability with Amazon CloudWatch, AWS X-Ray
Establish environment separation (dev/staging/production)
Implement progressive deployment strategies (blue/green, canary)

phase_6.name: Analytics and AI Enablement
actions: Build data pipelines with AWS Glue and Amazon Kinesis
Implement analytics with Amazon QuickSight and Amazon Athena
Integrate AI/ML services (Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Personalize)
Expose OpenAPI specifications for AI agent integration
Implement event-driven architecture for AI workflow triggers

recommended_actions.name: Optimization & Licensing Assessment
recommended_actions.trigger_reason: Portfolio contains multiple on-premises workloads requiring migration: IBM z/OS mainframe (payroll-system), Oracle Solaris (loan-calculator), self-managed Oracle 11g databases (loan-calculator, partner-soap), self-managed SQL Server instances (document-portal, timesheet-webforms, crm-desktop), and Windows Server 2003/2008 infrastructure. Customer has not quantified savings from migrating these workloads to AWS managed services.

recommended_actions.name: Migration Acceleration Program
recommended_actions.trigger_reason: Portfolio-scale modernization required across 11 services with Critical severity status in all seven pathways. Multiple on-premises workloads (mainframe, Solaris, Windows Server) need migration to AWS. 186 High-severity findings span all modernization pathways. This is a large-scale migration and modernization opportunity requiring credits, partner funding, and expert support.

recommended_actions.name: End of Support Migration
recommended_actions.trigger_reason: EOL software detected across 10 of 11 services: Windows Server 2003/2008, SQL Server 2005/2012, .NET Framework 2.0, Visual Basic 6.0, Adobe ColdFusion 8, Python 2.7, Django 1.4, Ruby 1.8.7, Rails 2.3, Java 5/6, Apache Struts 1.3, Node.js 0.10, Express 3.x, MongoDB driver 1.4.7, Oracle 11g, IBM DB2 v10, PostgreSQL 9.1, JBoss AS 5.1, WebLogic 10.3. No security patches available for any of these components.

recommended_actions.name: Mainframe Modernization
recommended_actions.trigger_reason: COBOL mainframe workload detected: legacy-payroll-system runs Enterprise COBOL 4.2 on IBM z/OS with DB2 for z/OS v10 (end-of-support April 2020), batch processing via JCL and CA-7 scheduler. PII (SSN, bank accounts) stored without encryption. Requires assessment for replatform or refactor using AWS Mainframe Modernization service.

recommended_actions.name: Experience-Based Acceleration
recommended_actions.trigger_reason: 11 services with triggered pathways and Not Ready/Needs Work classification. Multiple High-effort remediation items across all services requiring hands-on modernization experience with cloud-native architectures, containers, managed databases, and modern DevOps practices that the team likely lacks given the current state of the portfolio.
